descriptors.definition: This legislation regulates foreign exchange transactions, external trade, payments, and the orderly development of the foreign exchange market in India. It empowers the management of foreign exchange reserves through restrictions on capital and current account transactions and authorized dealings.
inclusion: Regulation of transactions between residents and non-residents
Overseas investments and foreign investments in India
Adjudication and compounding of offenses
exclusion: Domestic currency transactions without foreign exchange implications
Transactions handled outside authorized channels without statutory compliance
nearby_distinctions: Differs from the older Foreign Exchange Regulation Act (FERA) by focusing on management rather than strict criminal criminalization and control.

descriptors.definition: The Act governs foreign exchange transactions nationwide and extends its reach to offices and branches outside India owned or controlled by residents. Enforcement is carried out by a specialized Directorate of Enforcement under Section 36.
inclusion: Branches, offices, and agencies outside India owned or controlled by Indian residents
Investigation of contraventions by the Directorate of Enforcement
exclusion: Domestic tax enforcement matters governed by separate revenue statutes
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes overall policy control exercised by the Reserve Bank of India from operational investigation and enforcement handled by the Directorate of Enforcement.

descriptors.concept_name: Preamble Extent and Commencement of FEMA
descriptors.definition: The statute aims to consolidate and amend foreign exchange laws to promote external trade and maintain the domestic foreign exchange market. It applies across India and covers overseas offices owned or controlled by Indian residents starting from June 1, 2000.
inclusion: Territory of India
Foreign branches controlled by Indian residents
Contraventions committed outside India by applicable persons
exclusion: Purely domestic transactions with no cross-border or foreign currency elements
nearby_distinctions: Extends extraterritorial jurisdiction specifically to controlled foreign business establishments unlike standard domestic economic laws.

descriptors.definition: This provision outlines core legal terms including currency, foreign exchange, export, and current account transactions. It establishes the foundational dictionary for interpreting operational limits under the legislation.
inclusion: Currency notes, postal orders, and credit cards
Payments for foreign trade, services, and short-term banking credit
Provision of services from India to outside India
exclusion: Transactions altering foreign assets or liabilities classified under capital account definitions
nearby_distinctions: Differentiates current account transactions meant for ordinary business and living expenses from capital account transactions that alter foreign assets and liabilities.
source_ambiguities: Section 6(3) reference noted as deleted with effect from 15th October 2019.

descriptors.definition: Residential status under this statute depends on physical presence in India exceeding 182 days during the preceding financial year. Specific exceptions apply for employment, business, or uncertain stays abroad regardless of citizenship.
inclusion: Individuals residing in India for more than 182 days in the preceding year
Entities registered or incorporated in India
Domestic and foreign owned corporate branches
exclusion: Individuals staying abroad for employment, business, or uncertain duration despite physical presence thresholds
nearby_distinctions: Residency is determined strictly by duration and purpose of stay rather than nationality or citizenship.

descriptors.concept_name: Regulation and Management of Foreign Exchange Dealings
descriptors.definition: Section 3 imposes strict prohibitions on unauthorized foreign exchange dealings, unauthorized cross-border payments, and financial transactions linked to acquiring foreign assets. These restrictions ensure that foreign flows occur exclusively through permitted channels and authorized intermediaries.
inclusion: Transfers of foreign exchange or securities with non-authorized persons
Payments made to or on behalf of non-residents without proper banking channels
Financial arrangements securing rights to assets outside India
exclusion: Transactions executed with general or special permission from the Reserve Bank of India
nearby_distinctions: Prohibits peer-to-peer foreign exchange swaps even at favorable market rates if conducted outside authorized dealer networks.

descriptors.definition: An authorised person comprises dealers, money changers, or off-shore banking units empowered by the Reserve Bank to handle foreign exchange. They must strictly follow regulatory directives and verify customer declarations for transactions.
inclusion: Authorised dealers and money changers appointed by the RBI
Off-shore banking units operating within Special Economic Zones
exclusion: Off-shore banking units conducting direct transactions with domestic residents in India
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes standard authorised dealers serving general domestic residents from SEZ-based off-shore banking units restricted to principal-to-principal dealings.

descriptors.definition: Violations of statutory provisions, RBI directions, or authorization conditions attract monetary penalties up to three times the quantifiable sum involved or specific fixed amounts. Persistent offenses trigger additional daily fines, property confiscation, and potential imprisonment.
inclusion: Penalties up to three times quantifiable sums for general contraventions
Confiscation of domestic equivalents of foreign assets
Civil imprisonment for defaulting on large penalty payments
exclusion: Compliant transactions executed within authorized regulatory limits
nearby_distinctions: Separates administrative penalties and fines from criminal imprisonment terms applied under serious asset acquisition contraventions.

descriptors.definition: Authorized officers from the Enforcement Directorate or RBI can compound eligible contraventions within 180 days of receiving an application. Successful compounding bars any further legal or adjudicatory proceedings for that specific offense.
inclusion: Compounding applications processed within 180 days
Immunity from further proceedings upon successful compounding
exclusion: Offenses lacking formal compounding applications or falling outside statutory compounding rules
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes voluntary settlement through compounding from adversarial adjudication before a formal Adjudicating Authority.

descriptors.definition: Central Government-appointed Adjudicating Authorities hold inquiries and issue orders on complaints regarding statutory contraventions within a targeted one-year timeframe. Aggrieved parties can file appeals before designated appellate bodies and high courts within strict limitation periods.
inclusion: Inquiries conducted by appointed Adjudicating Authorities
Appeals to Special Director and Appellate Tribunal within 45 days
exclusion: Matters settled via compounding prior to formal complaint adjudication
nearby_distinctions: Separates first-instance inquiries by the Adjudicating Authority from subsequent appellate reviews handled by specialized tribunals and high courts.

descriptors.concept_name: Directorate of Enforcement and Investigative Powers
descriptors.definition: The Central Government establishes a Directorate of Enforcement staffed with specialized officers to investigate statutory contraventions. Authorized officers possess search, seizure, and investigative powers comparable to income-tax authorities.
inclusion: Establishment of the Directorate of Enforcement
Search and seizure powers for officers above assistant director rank
Empowerment of customs, excise, or police officers
exclusion: General civil litigations outside foreign exchange management scope
nearby_distinctions: Differentiates specialized enforcement officers from general administrative regulators within the Reserve Bank.

descriptors.definition: This provision governs evidentiary presumptions for documents produced, seized, or authenticated from foreign jurisdictions during investigations. Additionally, the Central Government holds authority to suspend or relax statute operations in the public interest.
inclusion: Presumptions regarding handwriting and document execution in proceedings
Admission of documents despite minor stamping omissions if otherwise admissible
Temporary or indefinite suspension of statutory provisions by notification
exclusion: Unauthenticated documents lacking statutory verification standards
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes routine evidentiary rules from extraordinary executive powers allowing total or partial suspension of economic laws in public interest.
